children.name: Pilostyles maya P.Ortega, Gonz.-Martínez & S.Vázquez
children.description: The native range of this species is Mexico (Campeche). It grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Pilostyles mexicana  Rose
children.description: The native range of this species is S. Mexico to Honduras. It is a holoparasite and grows primarily in the seasonally dry tropical biome.

children.name: Pilostyles thurberi A.Gray
children.description: Pilostyles thurberi is a species of endoparasitic flowering plant known by the common names Thurber's stemsucker and Thurber's pilostyles.

children.name: Pilostyles coccoidea
children.description:
4. Pilostyles coccoidea K.R.Thiele, Nuytsia 18: 273-284. 2008.

Type.

Australia, Western Australia, Waddi Road, 30°33'26"S, 115°28'10"E, 7 Mar. 2008, parasitic on Jacksonia, K.R. Thiele 3495 (PERTH 07692447).

Note.

Tepals pale orange to brown, in 2 whorls, flowers <3 mm in diameter. Growing in stems of Jacksonia in Western Australia (Figs 2 and 3, see Thiele et al. 2008 for pictures of flowers).

children.name: Pilostyles blanchetii
children.description: The native range of this species is Cayman Is., Jamaica, Mexico (Michoacán), Costa Rica to NE. Argentina. It is a holoparasite and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Pilostyles hamiltonii
children.description:
3. Pilostyles hamiltonii Gardner, J. Roy. Soc. Western Australia 32: 77. 1948.

Type.

Australia, Western Australia, Darling District, Helena Rover, Mundaring Weir, Mar. 1946, parasitic on Daviesia pectinata Lindl., C. D. Hamilton s.n. (PERTH, not seen).

Note: Tepals dark burgundy, in 2 whorls, flowers>3 mm in diameter. Growing in young stems of Daviesia in Western Australia (Figs 2, 3, see Thiele et al. 2008 for pictures of flowers).

children.name: Pilostyles haussknechtii
children.description:
6. Pilostyles haussknechtii Boissier, Arch. Sci. Phys. Nat. 25: 255-261. 1866.

Type.

Middle East, parasitic on Astragalus, J. E. Haussknecht s.n (G-BOISS, not seen).

Note: Tepals pink to brown in 2 whorls, each with 6 to 10 tepals (Fig. 6G). Found at the basis of young branches of Astragalus and occasionally Onobrychis and Halimodendron in Iran (Figs 2, 3).

children.name: Pilostyles boyacensis
children.description: Holoparasitic, monoecious plants. Flower cushions numerous, fusiform, oriented longitudinally. Flowers gregarious; floral buds initially developed in rows of 3 – 10 flowers; carpellate and staminate flowers often found on each row, but the former appear to be more frequent, tubular and almost cleistogamous. Outer and middle scales free and arranged in approximately two whorls of 5 (6) organs each, imbricate, widely oblong, 0.8 – 1.2 × 0.6 – 1.0 mm, purple, adaxially and abaxially finely grooved;

children.name: Pilostyles collina
children.description:
2. Pilostyles collina Dell, Nuytsia 4: 293-294. 1983.

Type.

Australia, Western Australia, Peak Charles, 10 Jan. 1982, parasitic on Oxylobium, B. D. Dell 8216 (G, MO).

Note: Tepals orange to red, in 3 whorls. Growing in young stems of Gastrolobium and Oxylobium in Western Australia (Figs 2, 3, see Thiele et al. 2008 for pictures of flowers).
